questions: Do symptoms follow specific exposures like foods, pollen, dust, mold, animals, NSAIDs, or alcohol?
Any hives, flushing, wheeze, swelling, throat tightness, or anaphylaxis history?
Any eczema, asthma, chronic congestion, or seasonal rhinitis?
Which foods trigger symptoms, and how quickly?
Constipation, diarrhea, reflux, bloating, pain, blood, weight loss, or nocturnal symptoms?
Any family history of celiac, IBD, gallstones, or liver disease?
Power, endurance, or mixed training response history?
Any recurrent cramps, rhabdomyolysis, dark urine, or severe exercise intolerance?
How quickly do soreness, sleep, HRV, and performance recover after hard training?
Are symptoms cyclic and strongest in the luteal phase?
Do symptoms improve within a few days after bleeding starts?
What is the first day of bleeding, and on which cycle days do irritability, avoidance, anxiety, depression, pain, or physical symptoms begin and end?
Has this pattern been recorded prospectively every day across at least two cycles, including symptom-free days?
What is the exact contraceptive product, active ingredient(s), dose, schedule, and start date? Is it progestin-only or combined estrogen-plus-progestin?
Cycle regularity, acne, hair changes, cramps, pelvic pain, pain with sex, unusually heavy/prolonged bleeding, or fertility concerns?
red_flags: very heavy bleeding with dizziness, fainting, or weakness
possible pregnancy with pain or bleeding
confirmations: daily symptom tracking across at least 2 cycles
exact medication label or prescribing record
CBC and ferritin when bleeding is heavy or prolonged
TSH and other targeted tests when clinically indicated
transvaginal ultrasound or MRI when adenomyosis is suspected
gynecology and mental-health review when indicated

questions: Sunburn tendency, freckling, mole history, eczema, psoriasis, acne, scarring, hair thinning?
Triggers: UV, foods, stress, infections, products, hormones?
Fractures from low trauma, height loss, bone pain, delayed healing, family history of osteoporosis?
Dietary calcium/protein, vitamin D, resistance training, steroid use?
Kidney stones, gout attacks, blood pressure salt sensitivity, cramps, unusual thirst/urination?
Any abnormal creatinine, electrolytes, urinalysis, or family kidney disease?
Wheeze, cough, exercise shortness of breath, snoring, witnessed apneas, daytime sleepiness?
Smoke/vape, occupational exposures, allergies, recurrent infections?
Joint swelling, rashes, mouth ulcers, fevers, gut inflammation, thyroid symptoms, neurologic episodes?
Family history of autoimmune disease?
Migraine pattern, aura, photophobia, nausea, triggers, pain sensitivity, medication response?
Taste/smell/sensory sensitivities or neuropathic pain?
What are the most recent A1C, fasting glucose, triglyceride, blood-pressure, and liver-test results, and when were they measured?
Any increased thirst or urination, unusual fatigue, post-meal symptoms, fatty-liver history, or prior gestational diabetes?
What do sleep, activity, meal timing, alcohol, and medication patterns look like around the symptoms or lab changes?
Is there a family history of diabetes, severe triglycerides, fatty liver, or early cardiovascular disease?
red_flags: confusion or fainting with suspected glucose symptoms
rapidly worsening symptoms with very abnormal laboratory results
confirmations: 2-hour oral glucose tolerance test when clinically indicated
fasting lipid panel and targeted liver tests
clinician review of blood pressure, medications, and overall risk

questions: What are the recent home or clinic blood-pressure readings and the full lipid panel, including LDL-C, HDL-C, triglycerides, and non-HDL-C?
Has Lp(a) or ApoB ever been measured, and is there a family history of early heart attack, stroke, aortic disease, or very high cholesterol?
Any exertional chest pressure, unusual shortness of breath, palpitations, fainting, leg swelling, or neurologic episodes?
What medications, nicotine exposure, sleep pattern, activity, and pregnancy-related or inflammatory conditions are clinically relevant?
red_flags: new one-sided weakness, facial droop, or trouble speaking
confirmations: one-time Lp(a) measurement and selective ApoB discussion when clinically appropriate
clinician-guided cardiovascular risk assessment rather than a SNP score

questions: Have TSH, free T4, or thyroid-antibody results been measured, and what were the dates, units, and laboratory ranges?
Any persistent cold or heat intolerance, palpitations, tremor, bowel or weight change, neck swelling, hair/skin change, or menstrual change?
Are thyroid medication, biotin, iodine, selenium, or other supplements being used, and what are the exact products and timing?
Any personal or family history of autoimmune thyroid disease, thyroid nodules, radiation exposure, or postpartum thyroid symptoms?
red_flags: chest pain, fainting, or sustained rapid heartbeat
rapidly enlarging neck swelling or trouble breathing/swallowing
new severe symptoms during pregnancy or shortly after delivery
confirmations: TSH and free T4 interpreted by a clinician
thyroid antibodies or ultrasound when clinically indicated
medication and supplement timing review before interpreting discordant results
repeat or specialist evaluation when symptoms and labs do not agree

questions: What are the usual sleep and wake times on workdays and free days, and how long does falling asleep or staying asleep take?
Any loud snoring, witnessed breathing pauses, gasping, morning headaches, unrefreshing sleep, or daytime sleepiness?
How do shift work, light exposure, caffeine, alcohol, medications, stress, pain, and cycle or hormone timing affect sleep?
Does sleepiness affect driving, operating equipment, school, work, or safety?
red_flags: near-miss or crash caused by sleepiness
repeated witnessed breathing pauses or choking during sleep
severe sleep loss with confusion or inability to function safely
chest pain or fainting associated with nighttime breathing symptoms
confirmations: sleep diary or wearable record used as context rather than diagnosis
validated sleep-apnea screening followed by clinician review
home sleep-apnea test or polysomnography when indicated
medication, substance, mood, pain, and thyroid review when sleep is persistently impaired

questions: What exact medication, active ingredient, formulation, dose, indication, start date, and schedule are being considered or taken?
What benefit, side effect, allergy, treatment failure, or unusual sensitivity occurred, and when did it begin relative to the dose?
Which other prescriptions, over-the-counter products, supplements, alcohol, or smoking exposures could affect the medication?
Is there a complete clinical PGx result with a diplotype or phenotype, or only one or a few consumer-array SNPs?
red_flags: trouble breathing, facial swelling, or widespread blistering rash after a medication
unusual bleeding, severe sedation, confusion, or fainting
high fever or severe muscle symptoms after a medication
suspected overdose or rapidly worsening adverse effect
confirmations: clinical-grade PGx testing when a prescriber considers it relevant
complete diplotype, copy-number, and phenotype assessment where required
current drug label plus CPIC, FDA, or pharmacist review
do not start, stop, or change a medication from a consumer SNP result alone

questions: Which symptoms are present, when did they begin, and how do sleep, stress, pain, substances, medications, and life context change them?
Are attention, organization, mood, anxiety, sensory sensitivity, headaches, or impulse-control concerns present across more than one setting?
What was the developmental, educational, work, and family history, and what strategies or treatments have helped or harmed?
Are any symptoms clearly cyclic, episodic, medication-related, or new rather than lifelong?
red_flags: suicidal thoughts or immediate safety concerns
new confusion, weakness, seizure, or severe neurologic change
several nights with little sleep plus unsafe behavior or loss of reality testing
rapidly worsening symptoms after starting or stopping a medication
confirmations: sleep, thyroid, substance, medication, and relevant laboratory review
collateral or longitudinal information when symptoms vary by setting
urgent mental-health or neurologic care when red flags are present

questions: Any joint hypermobility, recurrent sprains, dislocations, instability, chronic pain, or unusual recovery after injury?
Any unusually stretchy or fragile skin, abnormal scarring, easy bruising, hernias, pelvic-organ prolapse, or dental/bone fragility?
Any family history of aortic aneurysm/dissection, sudden unexplained death, severe eye findings, or a diagnosed connective-tissue disorder?
Which findings are clinician-observed versus self-described, and have imaging or prior genetic reports been reviewed?
red_flags: sudden severe chest, back, or abdominal pain
fainting with exertion or new neurologic symptoms
acute limb numbness or loss of circulation after a dislocation
rapidly progressive weakness or breathing difficulty
confirmations: physical examination using an appropriate hypermobility or connective-tissue assessment
echocardiography or vascular imaging when clinically indicated
clinical genetics review for syndromic features or family history
targeted clinical sequencing rather than common SNP interpretation when a disorder is suspected
